headline: Corn drops nearly 4% Friday on WASDE; cattle hold the gains
lead: Corn settled at $4.80 Friday, down almost 20 cents, after WASDE numbers came in heavier than the trade wanted. Cattle didn't blink, closing at $224.60, up 1.2% on the week. Every bushel still in the bin is worth less than it was Thursday morning.
teaser: Corn took a hard hit on WASDE Friday while cattle and feeders kept climbing.

one_number.unit: soybean meal's spot in its 52-week range
one_number.context: Meal sits near the top of its yearly range even as corn and wheat got cut hard Friday.

sections.title: Corn takes the WASDE hit
sections.body:
- Corn fell 19¾ cents to **$4.80**, down 3.9% on the day, after Friday's WASDE report leaned heavier than expected.
- Oats dropped with it, off 3.1% to $4.20, and Chicago wheat lost 1.8% to $6.71, so the cut wasn't corn alone.
sections.so_what: Corn absorbed the bad number; beans shrugged it off entirely.

sections.title: Cattle and feeders close the week strong
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$224.60**, up 1.2%, and feeders gained 1.7% to $343.90.
- The Cargill lockout, running since May 19, still has roughly 6,000 head a day of processing capacity off the table, and packer margins rather than cattle supply remain the squeeze.
sections.so_what: Cattle keep climbing on tight processing capacity, not a bigger herd.

outside_the_pit.title: HPAI confirmed in two Washington dairy herds
outside_the_pit.body: APHIS confirmed H5 avian flu in two Washington dairy herds Friday, the latest reminder the virus hasn't left the dairy sector.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress report. Corn and soybean harvest pace matters more than usual after Friday's WASDE cut.
Corn back above $4.90 would say Friday's drop was overdone; staying under $4.80 says the market believed it.
Export sales. A soybean number over 1.5 MMT would back up the strength that shrugged off WASDE.

source_summary: USDA WASDE, CME settlement data, APHIS, EIA

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $5.01 vs $4.62 projected (+8.4%), 7 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.89 vs $11.09 projected (+16.2%), 5 of 22 trading days in.
